head: d518ab6
target: The runner refuses a secret or model key shorter than eight characters as a scenario problem, before the first session opens, so the scrub cannot corrupt the run log with a short value.
incidental: test fixtures use secret and key values that meet the new floor, and cover a short pair
the design doc states the new refusal in the fail-before-paying invariant and the verification list

questions.prompt: Before this change, why did a one-letter secret value make the whole run fail at the end?

options.label: The model refused the run, because it cannot sign calls with a one-letter key.
The scrub marks the letter wherever it appears, keys included, so the run's files stopped parsing.
The runner treated the short value as unset, and dropped it from the log.
The letter leaked into the log, and the leak check failed the run.

key_points: The scrub replaces the raw value wherever it appears in the log, keys included.
It cannot tell a real leak from the same letters inside an ordinary word.
A one-letter value rewrites many words and keys, so the run cannot read its own files back.

questions.prompt: Before this change, a short secret failed the run at the end. Why does the runner now refuse it before the first session opens?
key_points: The refusal stops the run before the first session opens, so no model call is spent.
The old failure came at the end, after the run had already spent model calls.

questions.prompt: Which of these does the runner refuse before the first session opens?

options.label: A model key of seven characters
A secret of exactly eight characters
A secret that is not set
A twenty-character secret whose value is a common word

key_points: The length floor also covers the model key, because the scrub reads it like any secret.
Only values shorter than eight characters are refused; eight itself is allowed.
A long value passes the floor, so a collision with ordinary text stays possible but unlikely.
